text.text_excerpt: I love this place. It's intimate and always has wonderful musicians playing. I love how off the beaten path it is, not everyone knows about it. I hadn't been in a while, so I was happy to go when my friend suggested the show. You walk in the door and are transported from the street (where the place doesn't look like much) and receive a warm welcome. The music venue part of the bar is to the side of the bar (haha right) and is almost like another room. It's pretty big once you actually walk around the corner. There's a lot of chairs so you can sit by the music! There's also couches and sitting area in the bar area. We had blood orange margaritas which were delicious and strong! We listened...

Loved this place. Heard master artist/cellist Helen Gillet last night. So relaxed and close up. Wow. People behind the bar were friendly. Hearing such great music for a suggested donation of $10 which you put into a Can at the front when you were so inclined - in other words very laid back and truly suggested not mandated. Loved the cozy outer room with sofas, too.

I haven't been here in a while and definitely need to go back. Keith was super nice and the drinks were great. I also tried the turkey sandwich and it was pretty good but the shining start were the house potato chips. He pulled them out of this brine and dropped them in the grease and they were SO good. It's a small spot and has a lot of musicians and poets come to perform, which I think is great. It's beside the Tulane and Broad courthouse (criminal court). I first noticed it when I was interning at the district attorney's office and thought that the name was super cute because it's a bar on the side of the court and because you ask the judge for a sidebar when you want to say something ...
